79948.subject: Not all revenue sharing is equal. Do buybacks beat dividends?
79948.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/27e7dada-7bb7-4fcb-8126-f9079f724579/Top_Zama.png?t=1790698426)
Follow image link: (https://defillama.com/research/report/zama-a-look-into-confidential-defi)
Caption: 

## Do buybacks or dividends perform better for DeFi tokens?

We learned 3 things from this analysis:

Analyze today’s Holders Revenue (https://defillama.com/holders-revenue?groupBy=monthly&chartView=Breakdown)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2ce13354-8950-4f20-b325-4e3e8c5c02d5/buyback-vs-dividend-tokens-ytd-return_2026-09-29__1_.png?t=1790691110)
Caption: 

1. Buyback tokens outperformed on average. +19.7% median vs +11.1% for direct distribution tokens.

2. Larger tokens performed better. Market cap vs YTD return has a strong correlation with the largest tokens in this dataset. Weighted by market cap, buyback returns explode to 190% vs direct distribution’s +29%.

3. Protocols that distribute a small portion of revenue underperformed protocols that didn’t share any revenue at all.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/27c1f501-5c76-4bab-9008-276145103480/median-ytd-return-by-revenue-retention-type_2026-09-29.png?t=1790693950)
Caption: 

A larger share of protocols distributing any revenue have positive price performance YTD compared to protocols that don’t share revenue.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fe914896-a3e5-4483-915f-6943046b8cde/image.png?t=1790693940)
Caption: 





## The Revenue landscape transformed over the last two years

The total number of protocols with Holder Revenue has increased dramatically over the last two years.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6ace5471-29b4-4293-89ec-bd4653579ea7/protocols-with-holder-revenue-monthly_2026-09-29.png?t=1790690570)
Caption: 

[Protocols have earned over $1b per month in total revenue](https://defillama.com/revenue?groupBy=monthly) for the last 23 months.

Holder revenue as a % of total protocol revenue is trending up. Two years ago, 5% of total protocol revenue went to holders.

After falling for the first half of this year, 15% of total protocol revenue is being distributed to holders.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9f798dbf-8bc3-4b38-b9ef-58db69bdb0ca/holder-revenue-as-of-total-protocol-revenue_2026-09-29.png?t=1790697523)
Caption: 

## September Revenue Trends

September is on pace to be the largest month for total holders revenue [since January](https://defillama.com/holders-reven

79944.subject: Tokenization Briefing: Tokenized Stock Holders grew 43x YoY
79944.body:
The Tokenization Briefing newsletter keeps you up to date with market insights and visual analyses on what matters in the world of tokenized assets

( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/tokenization-briefing )

GM. Two weeks after the CLARITY Act failed in the Senate, regulatory agencies continue to move the market forward by adapting existing rules to onchain assets. Last Thursday, CFTC staff confirmed that futures brokers and clearinghouses can hold customer money in tokenized Treasuries, allowing tokenized assets to tap into $442.7 billion of customer margin.

In today’s issue, we cover the CFTC’s update regarding tokenized Treasuries, a 43x increase in tokenized stock holders alongside a new industry coalition, and tokenized gold's return above $5 billion as a regulated lender begins accepting it as loan collateral.

Thanks for subscribing!

*Top of Mind*

*The CFTC Opens FCM Customer Accounts to Tokenized Collateral*

On September 24, three CFTC divisions confirmed that futures commission merchants (FCMs) and derivatives clearing organizations can invest segregated customer funds in tokenized versions of the instruments allowed by Regulation 1.25. Tokenized assets need to match the legal and economic rights of the underlying instruments and pass the rule’s liquidity, concentration, maturity, and custody tests.

It came two days after Chairman Michael Selig told the Treasury Market Conference at the New York Fed that regulators need to prepare markets for “mass tokenization,” singling out tokenized assets used as collateral as one of the most important developments.

U.S. FCM funds reached a record $442.7 billion in February, an increase of 26% YOY. While these funds have long been permitted in Treasuries and government money market funds, their tokenized counterparts are now eligible too. The entire tokenized Treasury market currently represents just 3.3% of that customer fund pool.

If FCMs allocated 2.5% of customer funds into tokenized Treasuries, the market would grow by roughly 75% or ~$11B.

FCMs are cautious with customer money, so regulatory approval doesn't mean they'll actually adopt it. Products tailored for institutional collateral, such as BlackRock’s BUIDL, Circle’s USYC, and Franklin Templeton’s BENJI, will likely benefit the most.

*Charts & Charts*

*Tokenized Stock Holders Grew 43x in a Year*

Onchain holders of tokenized stocks reached 4.01 million on September 27, up from roughly 70K a year ago, according to RWA.xyz. Robinhood leads with 1.48 million holders, followed by bStocks with 1.40 million, and xStocks with 625,680.

As tokenized stocks increase in popularity and the debate around how they should be structured continues, the newly launched Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition aims to bridge the gap by tying tokenized shares directly to an issuer’s official shareholder register.
